Transform values between the native and the parameter scale of a link

Source: R/helpers-parameters.R
link_transform.Rd

link_transform() applies one of the links bmm uses for model parameters to a numeric vector. With inverse = FALSE it maps values from the native scale of a parameter, the scale of the model equations, to the parameter scale, the scale on which bmm() samples the intercept and coefficients of the parameter's formula. With inverse = TRUE it maps values from the parameter scale back to the native scale.

Usage

link_transform(values, link, inverse = FALSE)

Arguments

values

A numeric vector, matrix or array. With inverse = FALSE the values are on the native scale, with inverse = TRUE on the parameter scale. NA stays NA at its position.

link

A single string naming the link: "identity", "log", "softplus", "log1p", "logm1", "inverse", "sqrt", "logit", "probit", "tan_half", "loglog" or "cloglog". A NULL link is read as the identity link, as for a model parameter that declares no link.

inverse

Logical. FALSE (the default) transforms from the native to the parameter scale; TRUE transforms from the parameter scale to the native scale.

Value

The transformed values, with the length and dimensions of values (a matrix stays a matrix).

Details

The links, with the native values each accepts. x is a value on the native scale, eta one on the parameter scale.

linkinverse = FALSE: eta from xinverse = TRUE: x from etaNative values x
"identity"xetaall real numbers
"log"log(x)exp(eta)x > 0
"softplus"log(exp(x) - 1)log(1 + exp(eta))x > 0
"log1p"log(1 + x)exp(eta) - 1x > -1
"logm1"log(x - 1)exp(eta) + 1x > 1
"inverse"1 / x1 / etax != 0
"sqrt"sqrt(x)eta^2x >= 0
"logit"log(x / (1 - x))1 / (1 + exp(-eta))0 < x < 1
"probit"qnorm(x)pnorm(eta)0 < x < 1
"tan_half"tan(x / 2)2 * atan(eta)-pi < x < pi
"loglog"log(-log(x))exp(-exp(eta))0 < x < 1
"cloglog"log(-log(1 - x))1 - exp(-exp(eta))0 < x < 1

Values outside these ranges are not checked. For the links other than "tan_half", a value at an edge the range excludes, such as 0 for "log" and "inverse" or 1 for "logit", gives -Inf or Inf without a warning, and a value beyond it gives NaN (NA for "softplus") with a warning. "tan_half" reads x as an angle: a value outside -pi to pi gives the eta of the same angle inside that range, and returns that angle on the way back. "sqrt" squares on the way back, so a negative eta comes back as its absolute value: -3 gives 9, and 9 gives 3.

The table holds the links that transform one value at a time. It does not include "softmax", the link of the mixture weights of models such as mixture3p(): a softmax needs all weights of a group at once and a reference position, so link_transform() stops for it, as for any other name that is not in the table. parameter_info() shows the link of each parameter of a model in its link column; a parameter with "softmax" there is not covered by link_transform(). For the weights on the native scale, use native_parameters(). How the weights of a softmax group combine depends on the model, for mixture3p() on the set size (at set size 1 the non-target weight is zero), and native_parameters() applies that.

See also

parameter_info() for the link of each parameter of a model, and native_parameters() for the parameters of a fitted model on their native scale.

Examples

# a probability on the parameter scale of a logit link, and back
eta <- link_transform(c(0.2, 0.5, 0.8), "logit")
eta
#> [1] -1.386294  0.000000  1.386294
link_transform(eta, "logit", inverse = TRUE)
#> [1] 0.2 0.5 0.8

# the native value of a parameter with a log link, from its parameter scale
link_transform(c(-1, 0, 1), "log", inverse = TRUE)
#> [1] 0.3678794 1.0000000 2.7182818

# the link of each parameter of a model
parameter_info(sdm(resp_error = "y"))$link
#> [1] "tan_half" "log"      "log"
